This appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-claimant for enhancement of compensation awarded by V Additional Accident Claims Sugreev Singh Tomar vs Udham Singh Meena on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141309461/

sentences.text:
1 Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 72/2011 vide award dated 22/06/2012.
2.

Facts relevant and necessary for disposal of this appeal are to the effect that on 04/03/2011, when appellant/ injured was returning after closing his bakery from sharma farm road, char sahar ka naka and going to his home Indranagar on foot, a motorcyle bearing registration no. MP07-MK-5744 driven rashly and negligently dashed the appellant from behind.
Due to which, tibia fibula of his right leg came out and he also sustained grievous injuries on forehead, mouth, left leg and hands.
Thereafter, he was taken to Sahara Hospital, Gwalior where he was advised for immediate operation of both the legs.

Since he could not arrange the amount for operation, he was taken to Dr. D.
Prashad Private Nursing Home, Hazira, Gwalior where he was admitted from 04/03/2011 to 11/03/2011 where operation of his right leg was undertaken.

entities.text:
D.
Prashad Private Nursing Home, Hazira
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On the basis of aforesaid, case was registered at Crime No.218/2011.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant/ claimant submits that appellant was running a bakery shop registration of which was exhibited as Ex.P-31 and was earning Rs.1,58,000/- per year after deducting personal expenses.
Due to accident, appellant suffered 40% permanent disability.
Certificate of permanent disability was prepared by Dr. S.N. Tripathi, Medical Officer, Civil Hospital Board, Gwalior (PW-3), which was exhibited as Ex.P-33.

However, the tribunal has erred in not accepting the factum regarding permanent disability on the ground that the treating doctor Dr. D.
Prashad has opined that after operation of leg, the same was in good condition and the injuries suffered in his legs was recoverable.
It is further submitted that Rs.3,00,000/- has been spend during treatment but the tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- for expenditure of treatment which is on lower side.
Besides, Rs. 39,000/- has been awarded for medical bills and Rs.5000/- has been awarded under pain and suffering and Rs.5000/- has been awarded for special diet, which are also on lower side.
Therefore, the amount of compensation needs to be enhanced appropriately to work out the compensation.

4. Learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company supported the award and submitted that the tribunal after careful evaluation of the evidence placed before it has awarded the compensation, therefore, the same needs not to be interfered with.

5. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,49,000/- as compensation alongwith 6% interest per annum,
break-up of which is as under :-
 Medical Expenses - Rs.1,00,000/-
 Medicines - Rs.39,000/-
 Special Diet - Rs.5,000/-
 Pain and Suffering - Rs.5,000/-
 Total - Rs.1,49,000/-
6 . Heard.

7 . Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the impugned award, this Court is of the view that appellant could not prove the factum regarding permanent disability as certificate of PD was prepared by Dr. S.N. Tripathi, Medical Officer, Civil Hospital, Gwalior whereas the whole Sugreev Singh Tomar vs Udham Singh Meena on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141309461/
2 treatment and operation was undertaken by Dr. D. Prashad, who in his cross- examination has stated that after operation when he lastly examined the appellant, his legs were in good condition and he was advised to do exercise and take rest, hence, the disability was recoverable and cannot be said to be permanent disability.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, looking to the fact that during treatment, appellant remained hospitalized from 04/03/2011 to 11/03/2011 and has suffered physical and mental trauma, ends of justice shall be subserved if a lumsum amount of Rs.1,75,000/- (Rs. One Lac and Seventy Five Thousand only) is enhanced in addition to the amount awarded by the claims tribunal.

The enhanced amount of compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum as fixed by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of claim application till its realization, which shall be payable to the appellant/ claimant within 12 weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by Claims Tribunal while passing impugned award shall remain intact.
8. With the aforesaid, appeal stands allowed in part and disposed of.
No order as to cost.

(ROHIT ARYA) JUDGE vc VARSHA CHATURVEDI 2023.01.24 13:26:46 +05'30'
